review.findings_in_tested_scope: No new blocker found in the five tested boundaries. The prepare exception path sets _termination_unconfirmed inside the payload context, so a secondary context-close error cannot erase known creation uncertainty.
review.candidate_isolation: posthoc_completion.finish requires bound tree closure before reading candidate receipt/metrics or preparing artifact publication. Success uses attempt-local work files; mutable canonical metrics are published by the parent.
review.status_compatibility: Read-only inspection confirmed that normal adapter mappings without a status field are classified as completed by the fixed worker and accepted by the parent (status None is allowed). These five tests do not independently execute a successful native no-status completion; this claim is source review, not an extra passing case.
review.failure_semantics: Bound STOP/forced cleanup overrides an apparently successful worker result. Constructor and post-GO close-fault tests verify failed launch receipts, not scientific validity or task failure-report delivery.
review.import_boundary: posthoc_worker.main closes its payload FD before its explicit posthoc_runner/adapter import and invocation. This is not a sandbox claim: ordinary Python startup may execute permitted sitecustomize hooks before main. The temporary CPU fixture itself registers an adapter through sitecustomize. The guarantee must not be expanded to all Python startup hooks or arbitrary adapter imports. The supervisor uses isolated Python startup; these tests confirm that the adapter callable does not execute before GO.

additional_read_only_concerns.observation: In the tested candidate, float(cfg.get('posthoc_timeout', 3600)) is evaluated after READY/start accounting; NaN makes the elapsed > timeout comparison false. Recommend explicit finite-positive validation before intent if that is the chosen launch contract.
